content.safety_note: Always listen to your body. Stop immediately if you feel sharp pain (not to be confused with muscle burn). Ensure your incline push-up surface is stable and non-slip. Keep your core engaged during dead bugs to protect your lower back.

content.adaptation_note: As a beginner, focus on mastering form before increasing weight or intensity. If a session feels too easy, add one set to the main exercises. If it feels too hard, reduce the number of sets by one. Ensure you are getting adequate rest between sessions to allow for muscle recovery.
content.safety_note: Always listen to your body. Stop any exercise if you feel pain (not to be confused with muscle burn). Ensure you have a stable surface for incline push-ups and use appropriate dumbbell weights that allow you to complete the reps with good form.

content.adaptation_note: The plan focuses on low-impact movements to accommodate knee discomfort. Incline push-ups reduce load on the upper body, while glute bridges and dead bugs strengthen the core and hips without stressing the knees. Walking provides gentle cardio. If knee pain persists, reduce range of motion or substitute with seated variations where possible.
content.safety_note: Always warm up before starting. Stop any exercise that causes sharp pain. Consult a healthcare provider if knee discomfort worsens. Maintain proper form to prevent injury.
